root.name: King's Gambit Accepted: Philidor Gambit
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. f4 exf4 3. Nf3 g5 4. Bc4 Bg7 5. h4

overview: White continues 4.Bc4 Bg7 5.h4 h6 6.d4 d6 7.Qd3, building a pawn centre while Black has the extra pawn on f4. White aims to break with e5 or Nc3 and exploit Black's advanced kingside pawns, while Black tries to consolidate.

white_ideas.idea: Build a central pawn mass with d4, Qd3 and Nc3
Use the h-file and the bishop on c4 against the Black king

typical_structures.structure: White pawn centre against Black's advanced kingside pawns

character.notes: A classical King's Gambit line with mutual weaknesses.

gambit.notes: White gave the f-pawn and Black can keep it by holding the kingside.

soundness.notes: Theory prefers Black, but White gets real play and it is not refuted.

structure.notes: Open centre with the e-file in play.

level.notes: Lines to know plus the plans.

character.reason: Both sides take risks with exposed kings and tactics.

gambit.reason: White has given the f-pawn which Black can keep.

soundness.reason: Playable and not refuted, though Black is theoretically better.

structure.reason: Pawns are exchanged on f4 and the e-file opens.

level.reason: Theory matters but the lines are not very deep.

plans.reason: White must use development to attack as the pawn is down.
